Prior paper: R1 Zhao et al., When Debate Helps (2026)
Experimental intervention: Freeze mixed correct/wrong proposals; vary correct support, length-matched answer-stripped rationales, and neutral/withheld/shuffled controls.
Mechanism identified: Separates proposal supply from truth-sensitive readout.
Dataset and evidence regime: GPQA/MMLU-Redux controlled probes; mathematical and reasoning benchmarks for societies.
What it already establishes: Correct peer evidence can change selection without changing candidates; proposal-hit headroom and damage/recovery decomposition.
What it does not establish: Retrieved Web-source ownership or source-to-claim provenance integrity is not the controlled object.
Is our proposed finding distinct?: A alone is redundant. B without a source-specific failure mechanism is a close extension; binding remains unestablished.
Strength of supporting evidence: Strong direct overlap: full text §3.1, §5 controlled probes, A.9 Tables 8–10; reported experiments not reproduced.

Scientific question: Can complementary evidence views improve RAG?
Experimental intervention: Summary/extraction/reasoning agents process D; optional candidate-answer stage precedes synthesis. Ablate Answer Agent, retrieval depth and individual filters.
Mechanism identified: Evidence-view complementarity and synthesis; component ablations, not a frozen-proposal access effect.
Dataset and evidence regime: TriviaQA, PopQA, ARC-C, ASQA; fixed released retrievals, top 5/10.
What it already establishes: Evidence-centered multi-agent synthesis and intermediate candidates already exist.
What it does not establish: Output-selected unique-evidence subsets do not establish source necessity independently of model outcomes; no binding-only intervention.
Is our proposed finding distinct?: Generic B is crowded. A controlled provenance effect could differ, subject to attribution literature.
Strength of supporting evidence: Full paper §3.1 Eq. 1–6, §4.4, §4.5 Tables 3–5. Table 3 contradicts blanket improvement prose for PopQA/Mistral.

Prior paper: R3 Choi et al., Debate or Vote (2025)
Scientific question: How much debate gain is ensembling?
Experimental intervention: Compare initial majority with several debate topologies/rounds; oracle locks correct answers; conformist/follower retain or adopt majority.
Mechanism identified: Ensembling versus interaction; correctness preservation under update rules.
Dataset and evidence regime: Seven main NLP benchmarks; larger/persona/open-ended extensions; no retrieved-source manipulation.
What it already establishes: Vote is a strong comparator in tested settings; preservation interventions can alter revision outcomes.
What it does not establish: DCM martingale assumptions are not a universal impossibility theorem for evidence-informed debate.
Is our proposed finding distinct?: A preservation/consensus observation is not novel by itself. Web evidence intervention would be a different object.
Strength of supporting evidence: Official proceedings full paper §§2–5, especially 5.1–5.2; oracle explicitly nondeployable.

Prior paper: R4 Ai et al., Beyond Majority Voting (2026)
Scientific question: Can reliability and correlations improve aggregation?
Experimental intervention: Replace majority by OW/ISP and practical OW-L/OW-I using accuracy/cross-agent conditional-prediction information.
Mechanism identified: Aggregation gains from agent heterogeneity and higher-order information, under stated model assumptions.
Dataset and evidence regime: Synthetic, UltraFeedback, MMLU, ARMMAN; finite-label predictions.
What it already establishes: Improved readout does not require debate or more candidate generation.
What it does not establish: No controlled Web evidence-access, citation entailment, or provenance assignment experiment.
Is our proposed finding distinct?: A merely improving aggregate accuracy is redundant; B/C need an evidence-specific contrast.
Strength of supporting evidence: ICML proceedings identity; original full text §§2–5, Algorithms 1–2, Tables 2–3. No reproduction.

Scientific question: Which communication can be removed economically?
Experimental intervention: Policy-gradient spatial/temporal masks with low-rank regularization; one-shot magnitude pruning; topology, plug-in and attack evaluations.
Mechanism identified: Learned communication redundancy reduction, not source grounding.
Dataset and evidence regime: MMLU, GSM8K, MultiArith, SVAMP, AQuA, HumanEval; reasoning/code.
What it already establishes: Sparse topology and token-efficiency tradeoffs are established method territory.
What it does not establish: Pruning is not proof that a recipient used a particular source; edge savings need not equal saved physical calls.
Is our proposed finding distinct?: Generic sparse communication or cheaper collaboration is insufficient; a matched source-access mechanism may differ.
Strength of supporting evidence: ICLR venue verified; full original preprint §§2–4, especially 3.1–3.3 and 4.2–4.4. Proceedings PDF fetch failed.

Prior paper: R6 Li et al., Diverse Evidence / InfoDelphi (2026)
Scientific question: Does designed evidence asymmetry improve forecasting?
Experimental intervention: Same pre-retrieved union; BM25 shared public pool plus disjoint round-robin private pools. Vary public ratio, rationale exchange, rounds, routing and aggregation.
Mechanism identified: Private/shared evidence diversity plus rationale transfer; configuration effects.
Dataset and evidence regime: PolyGym 375 binary prediction-market questions, fixed evidence.
What it already establishes: Same-union evidence allocation and rationale exchange already have direct prior art.
What it does not establish: No independently necessity-qualified cross-document cohort, frozen proposal readout or binding-only intervention in inspected protocol.
Is our proposed finding distinct?: C is not novel as information asymmetry. Same union alone adds no distinction.
Strength of supporting evidence: Full text §3.3 Eq. 3–6; §5.2 Table 2; E.2. Public-ratio changes local context exposure.

Scientific question: How should RAG handle ambiguous/conflicting sources?
Experimental intervention: One agent per document; multi-round aggregator feedback; ablate aggregator/discussion and vary supporting/misinformation imbalance.
Mechanism identified: Document-grounded debate and conflict aggregation; system-level ablations.
Dataset and evidence regime: AmbigDocs, FaithEval, RAMDocs 500; ambiguous answers, synthetic misinformation and noise.
What it already establishes: Multi-agent source-grounded selection among conflicting responses already exists.
What it does not establish: No fixed candidate and fixed source-text provenance-binding contrast in inspected design; source imbalance is a different intervention.
Is our proposed finding distinct?: B as generic evidence-backed conflict resolution is redundant; a narrow causal binding study might differ.
Strength of supporting evidence: Full text §§3–4,6.1–6.3; arXiv v2 identifies COLM 2025. Official PDF browser challenge limits final-version comparison.

Prior paper: R8 Shen et al., Information Propagation (2025)
Scientific question: How does topology spread errors versus insights?
Experimental intervention: Manipulate one agent output/prompt; inject incorrect/correct signals while varying graph sparsity. CAPE/TCTE quantify final correctness flips.
Mechanism identified: Topology-dependent error/insight propagation under specified interventions.
Dataset and evidence regime: MMLU mechanism probes, originally correct/incorrect cohorts; broader method benchmarks.
What it already establishes: Causal output perturbation and propagation analysis predate this study.
What it does not establish: No Web-source necessity or evidence-to-candidate binding intervention.
Is our proposed finding distinct?: Do not claim first causal communication study; source grounding could be a different intervention.
Strength of supporting evidence: EMNLP venue; full original text §3.1 Eq. 5–6 and 3.2.1–3.2.2. Outcome-selected probe cohorts limit population interpretation.

Experimental intervention: Retrieval debate modifies query pool; response debate gives retrieved context to proponent, internal knowledge to challenger, then judge selects.
Mechanism identified: Asymmetric retrieval roles and adversarial response revision as a pipeline.
Dataset and evidence regime: NQ, TriviaQA, PopQA, 2Wiki, HotpotQA, StrategyQA; retrieval and response components.
What it already establishes: Retrieved versus internal-knowledge asymmetry already appears in multi-agent RAG.
What it does not establish: Pipeline gains do not isolate a binding-only or same-frozen-candidate provenance effect.
Is our proposed finding distinct?: Generic B/C is not distinct just because source access differs.
Strength of supporting evidence: Official full paper §3.3 Eq. 9–13; §5.5 Table 5 removes information asymmetry by giving all agents retrieval access.

Prior paper: R10 Wallat et al., Correctness is not Faithfulness (2024/2025)
Scientific question: Do correct citations reflect actual use?
Experimental intervention: Plant short model-answer snippets into other documents and rerun; analyze recovered answers and their citations.
Mechanism identified: Post-rationalization diagnostic distinguishes support from causal reliance.
Dataset and evidence regime: Attributed RAG with document substitutions; answer-recovery conditioning.
What it already establishes: Citation correctness is insufficient for faithfulness; content transplantation is prior causal attribution work.
What it does not establish: No fixed candidate multiset with entirely unchanged source bank; internal-process invariance remains a caveat.
Is our proposed finding distinct?: A binding-only selector effect would differ operationally, but is not yet a proven substantive advance.
Strength of supporting evidence: Root primary full-text inspection §§4–6; arXiv 2412.18004v1; author conference PDF header identifies ICTIR 2025.

Scientific question: Can source-induced answers be falsely attributed?
Experimental intervention: Construct/select malicious source text targeting a wrong answer and unsupported trusted citation while correct evidence remains; deletion checks and counterfactual defense.
Mechanism identified: Citation laundering and mismatch between causal driver and attributed support.
Dataset and evidence regime: Multi-source/multi-hop QA; source-level attack and defense.
What it already establishes: Unsupported trusted citations can accompany causally source-driven wrong answers.
What it does not establish: Does not freeze both candidate multiset and all source text; attack content changes.
Is our proposed finding distinct?: Target swaps with frozen texts are a different controlled object; novelty and WWW significance remain unestablished.
Strength of supporting evidence: Root full-text §§3–5, especially 4.1; original Sep 14,2026 preprint, not independently peer-reviewed/reproduced.

Prior paper: R12 Abolghasemi et al., Attribution Bias (2025)
Experimental intervention: Mixed-RAG counterfactuals preserve documents and swap human/AI authorship labels; compare answer EM and attribution metrics.
Mechanism identified: Metadata sensitivity and authorship-related attribution bias.
Dataset and evidence regime: Generator-aware RAG, three LLMs, mixed source authorship.
What it already establishes: Fixed content plus metadata-only intervention is already an experimental design in attribution research.
What it does not establish: Not a frozen agent-candidate selector with degree-preserving candidate–source edge reassignment.
Is our proposed finding distinct?: Only the particular relational intervention differs operationally; significance and novelty remain unestablished.
Strength of supporting evidence: Root primary full text §§3–4 Mixed RAG; official Findings ACL 2025 identity.
